candidates.label: A
candidates.notes: All Japanese terms, readings, index numbers and page references match the image. The gloss for ～割 ('percent; tenths') is imprecise, since 割 means units of ten percent. Other glosses are accurate. Headers are plain text with bracketed icons, not markdown headings.

candidates.label: B
candidates.notes: Japanese text and readings are all correct. The gloss for 〜割 ('in tenths; percent') is imprecise. The first section icon is rendered as a memo emoji, inconsistent with the book icon in the image. Headers are plain text, not markdown headings.

candidates.label: C
candidates.notes: All Japanese terms, readings and indices are correct. Glosses are accurate, including 〜割 as 'ten percent; tenth'. A blank line is added before group 2, which is harmless. Headers are plain text, not markdown headings.

candidates.label: D
candidates.notes: All Japanese terms, readings and indices are correct. Glosses are accurate; 'general acceptance' for 市民権 is a valid dictionary sense (as in 市民権を得る), and 〜割 is correctly 'tenth; ten percent'. Line order follows the image closely. Headers are plain text, not markdown headings.

candidates.label: E
candidates.notes: The reading for 生物学的な is given as せいぶつがくてきな, but the image prints せいぶつがくてき; the な is inserted. 'ユニット3' loses the spacing of the original. Glosses are accurate, though 口べた has only a single gloss. A blank line is added before group 2.

rationale: All five candidates are complete and nearly identical in the Japanese text, so the ranking turns on small differences. D and C have no transcription errors and fully accurate glosses; D is placed first because it keeps the original line grouping without an added blank line. A and B both give an imprecise 'percent' gloss for 割, and B also uses the wrong icon for the first section header. E is last because it is the only one that alters printed Japanese, adding な to the reading of 生物学的な.
